# Tools & releases development notes

> CocoaPods, Git, static libraries, Xcode, testing, compatibility and release notes.

## Historical context

Historical development notes from 2015–2017. Their original publication dates and source attribution are retained; translation or catalog updates do not make the examples current.
The examples were not rerun for this reorganization. Old Swift syntax, APIs, dependencies, service addresses and App Store rules may be obsolete; check current official documentation before applying them.

## Articles by original publication date

- [Disabling and dimming third-party sign-in buttons when the app is not installed](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-05-18-disabling-and-dimming-third-party-sign-in-buttons-when-the-app-is-not-installed/index.md): Uses QQ and WeChat sign-in buttons to show how installation checks can determine whether a button is hidden, disabled or dimmed. It records the interface treatment used when the corresponding third-party app was unavailable. Originally published: 2015-05-18. Published in 2015. Its App Review context and third-party SDK calls are retained as historical records. The original does not clearly identify an author. Retained as a historical article.
- [Installing and using CocoaPods for iOS development](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-05-20-installing-and-using-cocoapods-for-ios-development/index.md): Starting with Ruby and CocoaPods installation, this article explains how to find dependencies, write a Podfile, install pods and open the generated workspace. It also records a fix for header completion, illustrating an early iOS dependency-management workflow. Originally published: 2015-05-20. Published in 2015. The examples use iOS 7.0, SDWebImage 2.0 and the Ruby mirror address used at the time. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [iOS App Store rejection cases and solutions: an ongoing record](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-05-22-ios-app-store-rejection-cases-and-solutions-an-ongoing-record/index.md): A collection of App Review issues involving crashes, background modes, third-party sign-in, in-app purchases and user content, with the responses used at the time. These historical rules and individual cases help identify categories of review problems. Originally published: 2015-05-22. These review records date from 2015. Recheck rule numbers and proposed remedies against current official requirements. The original does not clearly identify an author. Retained as a historical article.
- [An illustrated guide to implementing iOS in-app purchases](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-06-04-an-illustrated-guide-to-implementing-ios-in-app-purchases/index.md): An early end-to-end integration guide covering agreements, in-app purchase products, sandbox accounts and client code. It follows StoreKit product requests, the payment queue, transaction-state handling and receipt validation through the setup process. Originally published: 2015-06-04. Published in 2015. The implementation uses the older SKProductsRequest, SKPaymentQueue and verifyReceipt workflow. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Packaging an iOS static library as an .a file](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-06-10-packaging-an-ios-static-library-as-an-a-file/index.md): Records a workflow for building separate device and simulator static libraries in Xcode, inspecting their architectures with lipo and combining the .a files. It explains matching the target platform during testing and checking the resulting library. Originally published: 2015-06-10. Published in 2015. The packaging workflow builds device and simulator .a libraries separately. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Detecting device locking in an iOS app](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-07-31-detecting-device-locking-in-an-ios-app/index.md): Records SpringBoard lock-notification handling used to investigate a failure in an embedded game when the device locked. It preserves the troubleshooting approach and callback code; the conditions under which those interfaces may be used need separate verification. Originally published: 2015-07-31. Published in 2015. The example listens for com.apple.springboard lock-screen notifications. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Practical lessons from localising an iOS app](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-09-29-practical-lessons-from-localising-an-ios-app/index.md): Reviews translation-file organisation, button-label length, language-region identifiers and localised image names. It focuses on how the language identifier changes in iOS 9 affected logic that detected Chinese in a multilingual project. Originally published: 2015-09-29. Specifically records adaptation to the region codes added to language identifiers in iOS 9. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Integrating a Baidu Mobile SSP launch ad in one minute](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-12-26-integrating-a-baidu-mobile-ssp-launch-ad-in-one-minute/index.md): Records the historical integration of Baidu Mobile SSP splash ads, from platform registration and SDK import to system dependencies, compiler options and launch-time delegate callbacks. It follows the main steps for loading an ad during app startup. Originally published: 2015-12-26. Published in 2015, with iOS 9 compatibility settings and the Baidu SSP SDK of that period. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Bison's collection of solutions to common Git errors](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-12-28-bison-s-collection-of-solutions-to-common-git-errors/index.md): Collects index-lock errors and warnings about Git's default push behaviour, with error screenshots and the configuration commands used at the time. It supports reviewing troubleshooting by error type; inspect the current repository state before applying a command. Originally published: 2015-12-28. Records Git issues on Windows 7 and the default push settings used at the time. Git troubleshooting notes collected by Bison.
- [Preparing an iOS app for Apple Pay](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-02-18-preparing-an-ios-app-for-apple-pay/index.md): Records early Apple Pay project setup: enabling the capability, creating a Merchant ID and configuring payment-request properties. It also lists questions about country and currency codes; the demonstrated result comes from the simulator identified in the original article. Originally published: 2016-02-18. Mentions iOS 8.1 and discusses the contemporary context of mainland China, iOS 9.2 and iPhone 6. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Restoring old Xcode plug-ins after a version update](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-02-19-restoring-old-xcode-plug-ins-after-a-version-update/index.md): Documents historical fixes for plug-ins that stopped loading after an Xcode update or an accidental Skip Bundles selection. It checks compatibility UUIDs, edits plug-in Info.plist files and resets the loading choice. Originally published: 2016-02-19. Compares Xcode 7.1, 7.2 and 7.2.1 and concerns the plug-in loading mechanism used at the time. Originally credited to 许漠颜; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Xcode development tips from a SwiftGG discussion](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-02-26-xcode-development-tips-from-a-swiftgg-discussion/index.md): Collects Xcode techniques from a SwiftGG discussion: exception, symbolic and test-failure breakpoints; inspecting and changing variables during debugging; Quick Look; and reusable code snippets. Originally published: 2016-02-26. A record of a 2016 discussion. Debugger and language support are described as they existed at the time. Originally credited to bestswifter; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Publishing a library to CocoaPods](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-04-04-publishing-a-library-to-cocoapods/index.md): Records the process of publishing an open-source library: preparing the GitHub project, registering with trunk, writing a podspec, checking versions and tags, validating and submitting. It also explains commonly used specification fields. Originally published: 2016-04-04. Published in 2016. Commands and repository submission steps reflect the CocoaPods service as it worked then. Originally credited to WzxJiang; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Apple's Xcode testing documentation in Chinese, part 1](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-04-15-apple-s-xcode-testing-documentation-in-chinese-part-1/index.md): A Chinese translation of earlier Apple testing documentation covering XCTest project setup, test classes and methods, the test lifecycle, performance tests and UI tests. The test navigator illustrates running cases and inspecting their results. Originally published: 2016-04-15. The Chinese translation was published in 2016 and covers testing capabilities and interfaces in Xcode 5, 6 and 7. Apple testing documentation translated by 许漠颜, then edited and archived by Bison.
- [Apple's Xcode testing documentation in Chinese, part 2](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-04-15-apple-s-xcode-testing-documentation-in-chinese-part-2/index.md): Continues the Chinese translation of Apple's testing documentation with code coverage, command-line testing, Xcode Server continuous integration and UI test recording. It also discusses structuring testable code and migrating from OCUnit to XCTest. Originally published: 2016-04-15. The Chinese translation was published in 2016, primarily in the testing-tool context of Xcode 7, iOS 9 and OS X 10.11. Apple testing documentation translated by 许漠颜, then edited and archived by Bison.
- [Prompting users to review an iOS app](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-05-03-prompting-users-to-review-an-ios-app/index.md): Introduces the LBToAppStore review-prompt wrapper, using the app version, elapsed days and the user's previous choice to decide when to show a dialog. The response either opens the store or postpones the reminder, illustrating an early review-request workflow. Originally published: 2016-05-03. Published in 2016. The older reminder workflow uses UIAlertView, UIAlertController and a link to the store. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [What's new in iOS 10: SiriKit](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-06-19-what-s-new-in-ios-10-sirikit/index.md): Introduces SiriKit integration following WWDC 2016, from creating an Intents Extension to implementing intent handling and its interface. It explains how a spoken request is interpreted and passed to an app extension for the relevant response. Originally published: 2016-06-19. Explicitly targets iOS 10 and Xcode 8, preserving SiriKit's service categories and extension configuration from that period. Originally credited to Sindri; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Adding iOS 10 Push Notification Extensions in Xcode 8](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-09-21-adding-ios-10-push-notification-extensions-in-xcode-8/index.md): Records the process of adding iOS 10 notification extensions to an existing app in Xcode 8. It covers push capabilities, signing, Swift versions, architecture settings, and debugging and submission issues for Service and Content extensions. Originally published: 2016-09-21. The article explicitly uses Xcode 8 and iOS 10 and discusses the choice between Swift 2.3 and Swift 3.0. Originally credited to zhao0; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Xcode 8 and iOS 10 Compatibility Notes](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-09-22-xcode-8-and-ios-10-compatibility-notes/index.md): Collects migration notes on notifications, ATS, privacy permissions, and interface changes in Xcode 8 and iOS 10. It also records issues involving logging, fonts, list performance, plugins, and xib warnings, with links to official documentation. Originally published: 2016-09-22. These notes explicitly concern compatibility with Xcode 8 and iOS 10 and retain the issues and approaches recorded at that time. Originally credited to 判若两人丶; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Practical Automated Testing for iOS](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2017-04-05-practical-automated-testing-for-ios/index.md): Compares unit tests with UI automation and introduces XCTest, Quick, Nimble, KIF, and Appium. It discusses waiting, stubs and mocks, command-line execution, and testable code structure as foundations for maintainable tests. Originally published: 2017-04-05. The article explicitly uses Xcode 8.2.1. Framework capabilities and examples are described in that environment. Originally credited to 黄文臣; edited and archived by Bison.
